title: Odoo Pricing 2026: Plans, Hosting and Implementation
summary: Odoo pricing depends on three factors: how many users log in, where the system runs, and whether you need custom code. Use these to pick your tier.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Odoo costs and limits teams hit


Ask for an itemized quote and it exposes the costs the per-user price leaves out, and **the largest is usually the implementation hours** .


The list below tags each omitted cost as either Odoo source (stated in Odoo's own pages or docs) or partner practice (what implementers commonly charge or do), so you know which lines you can verify and which you must negotiate.


### Odoo implementation and partner hour pack costs


Buy hours and you buy them in packs, with the rate per hour falling as the pack grows.[Opsily](https://opsily.com/hosting/odoo/odoo-success-pack-pricing) lists the Starter 4h pack at 499 €, about 125 € an hour, which buys a scoping call and little else.


The Basic 25h pack is 2635 €, or about 105 € an hour. The Standard 50h pack is 4675 €, about 94 € an hour.


At 100 hours the discount stops. The Custom 100h pack is 8415 € and the Pro 200h pack is 16830 €, both about 84 € an hour, so a bigger pack buys no cheaper hours.


Estimate your hours first and buy the pack that covers them, not the largest one.


### Customisation limits by plan


Studio, Odoo's point-and-click customisation tool, covers fields, views and simple automations. Custom Python modules are a separate matter, and Odoo Online doesn't run them.


If a partner proposes code, ask which hosting option it requires, because that choice can change your bill more than the seat count. **Treat any quote that adds code to a hosted plan without naming the hosting move as incomplete.**


### Storage, upgrades and extra hosting


Plans include 100 GB of storage and 200 outgoing emails a day (Odoo source). A team sending order confirmations and marketing mail from one database can reach the email cap before it reaches the storage cap, so count your daily sends.


Then come upgrades between major versions, another cost. Under partner practice, a migration with custom fields is billed as project hours, not as part of the subscription.


Add-ons and extra apps are priced separately (Odoo source), and renewal true-ups (partner practice) bill any users added mid-term at the next renewal.


### Connecting Odoo to the rest of your stack


Confirm external API access in writing before you design around it. It depends on your plan, and Odoo has restricted it on some Online tiers.


If the API is available, a workflow tool can sit between Odoo and your other systems and move records on a trigger. That replaces custom code for many integrations, which keeps you out of the higher-priced hosting.


If the only gap is passing data between Odoo and one other tool, the way the tool meters usage matters more than its connector.[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) counts the run as the meter: 1 credit per flow run, however many steps sit inside it.


A sync broken into ten small, retry-friendly steps therefore costs the same as the two-step shortcut, while Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so every extra step you add for reliability shows up on the invoice.


The free plan's 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows mean this line stays out of your Odoo estimate.


If the API isn't available on your plan, the integration needs an upgrade or a partner build, and both belong in the quote.
